q-fruehe-hochkulturen-20#explanation: Built around 2560 BC, the pyramid at Giza consists of some 2.3 million stone blocks and was originally about 146 metres high.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-21#question: According to Egyptian belief, before which god did the dead have to answer at the judgement of the dead?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-21#explanation: Only those who passed the judgement could live on in the afterlife; mummification and grave goods were meant to preserve the body and provide for it.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-22#question: What was especially characteristic of Indus Valley cities such as Mohenjo-daro?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-22#choices.0: Right-angled streets and a drainage system
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-22#choices.2: Stepped temple towers of mud brick
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-22#choices.3: Walls made of huge, undressed stone blocks
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-22#explanation: These planned cities in present-day Pakistan and northwest India had baked bricks, wells and baths; their script has still not been deciphered.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-23#question: What does legend say about the origins of Sargon of Akkad?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-23#choices.0: He was suckled by a she-wolf
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-23#choices.1: He was a son of the sun god Ra
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-23#choices.2: He was abandoned as a foundling in a reed basket
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-23#choices.3: He was a prince from the Indus Valley
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-23#explanation: Historically Sargon probably began as cupbearer to the king of Kish before conquering Sumer around 2334 BC and creating Mesopotamia's first empire.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-24#question: In the Code of Hammurabi, what determined the severity of many punishments?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-24#choices.1: The social rank of those involved
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-24#explanation: An offence against a free man was punished more harshly than one against a slave; in part the principle of 'an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth' applied.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-25#choices.2: A stepped temple tower of mud brick
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-25#explanation: A shrine to the city god stood on its top; the ziggurat of Ur is the best preserved, and the biblical Tower of Babel goes back to the one in Babylon.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-26#question: Which archaeologist excavated the Royal Tombs of Ur in the 1920s?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-26#explanation: Woolley found a gold helmet, lyres, lapis lazuli jewellery, the Standard of Ur and dozens of servants buried with the rulers.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-27#question: From which library do the tablets of the Epic of Gilgamesh come that were rediscovered in London in 1872?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-27#choices.1: The library of Ashurbanipal at Nineveh
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-27#explanation: Ashurbanipal collected over 30,000 clay tablets in the 7th century BC; the eleventh tablet of the epic contains the famous flood story.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-28#question: Which king reunited Egypt around 2055 BC and founded the Middle Kingdom?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-28#explanation: After about 150 years of division, the ruler from Thebes united the country; the Middle Kingdom is regarded as the classical age of Egyptian literature, with works such as the Story of Sinuhe.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-29#question: What did the Hyksos bring to Egypt from Western Asia?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-29#explanation: Around 1650 BC the Hyksos took power in the Nile Delta; Ahmose I drove them out around 1550 BC and founded the New Kingdom.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-30#question: Where did the female pharaoh Hatshepsut send a famous trading expedition?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-30#explanation: Punt lay on the Red Sea; the expedition is depicted in reliefs in Hatshepsut's terraced temple at Deir el-Bahari near Thebes.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-31#question: For whom did Hatshepsut first act as regent before having herself crowned pharaoh?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-31#explanation: In images Hatshepsut wears the ceremonial royal beard; after her death many of her depictions and names were erased.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-32#question: Where can the famous bust of Queen Nefertiti be seen today?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-32#choices.0: In the Egyptian Museum in Cairo
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-32#choices.2: In the British Museum in London
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-32#choices.3: In the Neues Museum in Berlin
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-32#explanation: Ludwig Borchardt found the painted limestone bust in 1912 in the workshop of the sculptor Thutmose at Amarna; Egypt is demanding its return.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-33#question: Who discovered the almost unplundered tomb of Tutankhamun in 1922?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-33#explanation: In the Valley of the Kings Carter found over 5,000 grave goods, including the golden death mask, chariots and thrones.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-34#question: What was Tutankhamun's name before he restored the old gods?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-34#explanation: By changing his name from Aten to Amun, the young king turned away from Akhenaten's cult and restored the old religion.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-35#question: Where did Ramesses II have his famous rock-cut temples built?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-35#explanation: Ramesses II reigned for 66 years and built more than any other pharaoh, including the Ramesseum and the capital Pi-Ramesses.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-36#question: Which branch of arms dominated the Battle of Kadesh in 1274 BC?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-36#explanation: It is considered one of the largest chariot battles in history; Ramesses II narrowly escaped defeat but had it portrayed as a glorious victory.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-37#question: Who excavated Mycenae in 1876, believing he had found the world of Homer?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-37#explanation: Schliemann found shaft graves with gold masks; Arthur Evans, by contrast, excavated the Minoan palace of Knossos on Crete from 1900.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-38#question: Which language did the Linear B script, deciphered in 1952, turn out to record?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-38#explanation: Michael Ventris showed that the Mycenaeans used Linear B to administer stores, craftsmen and taxes; the older Minoan Linear A remains undeciphered.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-39#question: What is special about the language of the Hittites?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-39#choices.0: It was the first language written in an alphabet
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-39#choices.1: It is closely related to Sumerian
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-39#choices.2: It was written only in Egyptian hieroglyphs
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-39#choices.3: It is the oldest Indo-European language attested in writing
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-39#explanation: The Hittites wrote in cuneiform; in their capital Hattusa an archive of over 30,000 clay tablets with laws, treaties and myths was found.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-40#question: Which empire fell around 1200 BC in the Late Bronze Age collapse?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-40#explanation: Droughts, famines, earthquakes, revolts and attacks by the Sea Peoples also struck the Mycenaean palaces and trading cities such as Ugarit; Hattusa was abandoned.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-41#question: Why did iron win out over bronze after 1200 BC?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-41#choices.0: Iron ore was available almost everywhere
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-41#choices.2: Iron was softer and easier to shape
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-41#choices.3: Iron did not need to be forged
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-41#explanation: When the trade routes for tin collapsed, the more laborious smelting in bloomery furnaces became worthwhile; ploughshares, axes and swords became cheaper as a result.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-42#question: Which metals is bronze made of?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-42#explanation: Bronze is harder than pure copper; because tin was rare and came from places such as Anatolia, Iran or Afghanistan, it stimulated long-distance trade.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-43#question: Where did the Mesopotamians and Egyptians obtain the prized blue lapis lazuli?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-43#explanation: Lapis lazuli travelled thousands of kilometres; Lebanon, by contrast, supplied cedar wood, Nubia gold and ivory, and Cyprus copper.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-44#question: Which city did the Phoenicians found in North Africa?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-44#explanation: According to tradition, Carthage was founded from Tyre in 814 BC and later rose to become Rome's great rival.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-45#question: Which drink brewed from barley was part of everyday life in Mesopotamia and Egypt?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-45#explanation: All classes drank beer, while wine was a luxury; people ate it with bread, onions, lentils, dates and fish.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-46#question: On which river lay the heartland of China's Shang dynasty?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-46#explanation: The Shang ruled from about 1600 to 1046 BC; their royal tombs at Anyang bear witness to skilful bronze casting and chariots.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-47#question: What was usually used to pay for larger transactions in the Bronze Age Near East?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-47#explanation: Coins were not invented until the 7th century BC in Lydia; until then silver, grain or copper served as means of payment by weight.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-48#question: Which division still in use today goes back to Babylonian scholars?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-48#choices.2: Counting years from the birth of Christ
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-48#choices.3: The month of July with 31 days
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-48#explanation: The Babylonians calculated in base 60; the division of the circle into 360 degrees also goes back to them.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-49#question: What rights did women have in ancient Egypt?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-49#choices.0: They could own property and sue in court
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-49#choices.1: They could leave the house only with a male escort
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-49#choices.2: They were excluded from inheritance as a rule
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-49#choices.3: They were not allowed to conclude contracts
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-49#explanation: Compared with other cultures, Egyptian women had many rights, including in trade; some women, such as Hatshepsut, even ruled as pharaoh.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-50#question: Which god did the kings of Kush worship at their holy mountain, Jebel Barkal?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-50#explanation: The Kushites adopted hieroglyphs, pyramid tombs and the cult of Amun from Egypt but remained culturally independent.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-51#question: In which language did the great powers of the 2nd millennium BC write to one another, for example in the Amarna letters?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-51#explanation: Akkadian in cuneiform was the language of diplomacy from Egypt to Anatolia; envoys, gifts and marriage alliances linked the royal courts.
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-52#question: Which of these rulers reigned last?
q-fruehe-hochkulturen-52#explanation: Hammurabi ruled in the 18th century BC, Hatshepsut in the 15th, Ramesses II in the 13th and Tiglath-Pileser I from 1114 to 1076 BC.
q-gegenwart-01#question: Which treaty founded the European Union?
q-gegenwart-01#explanation: The Treaty of Maastricht, signed in 1992, came into force in 1993 and created the European Union.
q-gegenwart-02#question: Which device did Steve Jobs present in January 2007?
q-gegenwart-02#explanation: The iPhone came onto the market in 2007 and launched the worldwide triumph of the smartphone.
q-gegenwart-03#question: To what level is global warming to be limited under the Paris Climate Agreement?
q-gegenwart-03#choices.2: To well below 2 degrees, if possible 1.5 degrees
q-gegenwart-03#explanation: The 2015 agreement aims for well below two degrees and if possible 1.5 degrees compared with pre-industrial times.
q-gegenwart-04#question: Which British colony was handed over to China in 1997?
q-gegenwart-04#explanation: On 1 July 1997 Hong Kong passed to China under the principle of one country, two systems.
q-gegenwart-05#question: In which year did a majority of the British vote to leave the EU?
q-gegenwart-05#explanation: In the referendum of 23 June 2016, 51.9 percent voted for Brexit; the departure took place in 2020.
q-gegenwart-06#question: Which state became independent in 2011 as Africa's youngest state?
q-gegenwart-06#explanation: After a referendum South Sudan broke away from Sudan on 9 July 2011.
q-gegenwart-07#question: In which town did Bosnian Serb troops murder around 8,000 Muslim men and boys in July 1995?
q-gegenwart-07#explanation: The UN tribunal in The Hague classified the Srebrenica massacre as genocide.
q-gegenwart-08#question: Which international organization did China join in December 2001?
q-gegenwart-08#explanation: Joining the WTO opened the world markets to China and made the country the workshop of the world.
q-gegenwart-09#question: What does Malala Yousafzai campaign for above all?
q-gegenwart-09#explanation: Malala fights for girls' right to schooling and received the Nobel Peace Prize for it in 2014.
q-gegenwart-10#question: Which Australian prime minister apologized to the Stolen Generations in 2008?
q-gegenwart-10#explanation: On 13 February 2008 Kevin Rudd apologized in parliament for the removal of Indigenous children.
q-gegenwart-11#question: Which Ukrainian peninsula did Russia annex in 2014?
q-gegenwart-11#explanation: Russia occupied Crimea in February and March 2014 and incorporated it after an unrecognized referendum.
q-gegenwart-12#question: Which organization replaced the Organization of African Unity in 2002?
q-gegenwart-12#choices.0: The Economic Community of West African States
q-gegenwart-12#explanation: The African Union was founded in Durban in July 2002 and is headquartered in Addis Ababa.
q-gegenwart-13#question: Who developed the World Wide Web at the CERN research centre?
q-gegenwart-13#explanation: Berners-Lee put the first website online in 1991 and waived patents so that the Web would be open to everyone. This made the Internet usable for a broad public.
q-gegenwart-14#question: Which population group was the main target of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda?
q-gegenwart-14#explanation: Hutu militias murdered about 800,000 people in around 100 days, mainly Tutsi but also moderate Hutu. The UN afterwards set up a criminal tribunal for Rwanda.
q-gegenwart-15#question: Since which year have people in twelve EU countries paid with euro coins and notes?
q-gegenwart-15#explanation: On 1 January 2002 euro cash replaced national currencies such as the Deutschmark. The euro had already been introduced as book money in 1999.
q-gegenwart-16#question: Which terrorist organisation carried out the attacks of 11 September 2001?
q-gegenwart-16#explanation: Under their leader Osama bin Laden, terrorists flew hijacked planes into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon; almost 3,000 people died. The USA responded with the war in Afghanistan.
q-gegenwart-17#question: How many states joined the European Union in its eastern enlargement of 2004?
q-gegenwart-17#explanation: Besides eight former communist countries of Central and Eastern Europe, Malta and Cyprus joined. It was the largest enlargement in the EU's history.
q-gegenwart-18#question: Off which island was the epicentre of the earthquake that triggered the Indian Ocean tsunami in December 2004?
q-gegenwart-18#explanation: The quake off the north-west coast of Sumatra was one of the strongest ever recorded. The tsunami killed around 230,000 people in fourteen countries.
q-gegenwart-19#question: What caused the Fukushima nuclear disaster in 2011?
q-gegenwart-19#choices.0: An undersea earthquake followed by a tsunami
q-gegenwart-19#choices.2: A terrorist attack on the plant
q-gegenwart-19#choices.3: A plane crashing into the reactor
q-gegenwart-19#explanation: The tidal wave destroyed the emergency power supply, causing meltdowns in several reactors. Germany subsequently decided to phase out nuclear power.
q-gegenwart-20#question: Who was elected in 2008 as the first African American president of the United States?
q-gegenwart-20#explanation: Obama served from 2009 to 2017 and received the Nobel Peace Prize as early as 2009. His election was seen as a historic turning point in a country with a long history of segregation.
q-gegenwart-21#question: In which country did the Arab Spring begin at the end of 2010?
q-gegenwart-21#explanation: The self-immolation of street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi sparked mass protests, and President Ben Ali fled in January 2011. The protests quickly spread to Egypt, Libya and Syria.
q-gegenwart-22#question: Which ruler was overthrown by a US-led coalition in 2003?
q-gegenwart-22#explanation: The USA justified the war with alleged weapons of mass destruction that were never found. Iraq then sank into years of insurgency and civil war.
q-gegenwart-23#question: Whom did Vladimir Putin succeed as President of Russia around the turn of the millennium?
q-gegenwart-23#explanation: Yeltsin resigned on 31 December 1999, making Putin acting president; Putin won the election in March 2000. Gorbachev had been head of state of the Soviet Union.
q-gegenwart-24#question: By what name is the infrastructure programme that Xi Jinping announced in 2013 known?
q-gegenwart-24#explanation: Through ports, railways and roads, China aims to expand its links with Asia, Africa and Europe. Many partner countries took on debt with Chinese banks in the process.
q-gegenwart-25#question: Which disease killed more than 11,000 people in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone from 2014 to 2016?
q-gegenwart-25#explanation: It was the largest Ebola epidemic in history up to that point. It showed how hard it is for weak health systems to contain an outbreak.
q-gegenwart-26#question: Which three states formed the NAFTA free trade area in 1994?
q-gegenwart-26#explanation: NAFTA came into force on 1 January 1994; on the same day the Zapatista uprising began in Mexico. In 2020 the agreement was replaced by a new treaty.
q-gegenwart-27#question: With which guerrilla group did Colombia's government sign a peace agreement in 2016?
q-gegenwart-27#explanation: The agreement ended a conflict that had lasted more than fifty years. President Juan Manuel Santos received the Nobel Peace Prize for it in 2016.
q-gegenwart-28#question: Which head of government led New Zealand through the aftermath of the Christchurch attack in 2019?
q-gegenwart-28#explanation: After the far-right attack on two mosques that killed 51 people, her government swiftly tightened gun laws. Ardern was prime minister from 2017 to 2023.
q-gegenwart-29#question: Which country did Ellen Johnson Sirleaf lead from 2006 as Africa's first elected female head of state?
q-gegenwart-29#explanation: Sirleaf took over a country devastated by civil war and governed until 2018. In 2011 she received the Nobel Peace Prize together with two other women.
q-gegenwart-30#question: What is Wangari Maathai's Green Belt Movement known for?
q-gegenwart-30#choices.2: Campaigns against plastic waste in the sea
q-gegenwart-30#choices.3: Planting millions of trees in Kenya
q-gegenwart-30#explanation: Working mainly with women, the movement planted more than 30 million trees to fight soil erosion and poverty. Maathai became the first African woman to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in 2004.
q-gegenwart-31#question: Which movement did Greta Thunberg spark with her school strike in 2018?
q-gegenwart-31#explanation: The Swedish teenager first protested alone outside the parliament in Stockholm for stronger climate action. Soon millions of pupils worldwide were striking for the climate on Fridays.
q-gegenwart-32#question: Which country did former metalworker Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva govern as president?
q-gegenwart-32#explanation: Lula was president from 2003 to 2010 and reduced poverty with social programmes such as Bolsa Família. He took office as president again in 2023.
q-gegenwart-33#question: What was Volodymyr Zelensky's profession before his election as President of Ukraine in 2019?
q-gegenwart-33#explanation: Zelensky starred in the TV series "Servant of the People" as a teacher who unexpectedly becomes president. In 2019 he won the election by a large majority.
q-gegenwart-34#question: What did Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna receive the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for?
q-gegenwart-34#explanation: CRISPR-Cas9 makes it possible to alter genetic material precisely and relatively easily. It was the first time two women shared a Nobel Prize in a science category.
q-gegenwart-35#question: Which country does Pope Francis, elected in 2013, come from?
q-gegenwart-35#explanation: Jorge Mario Bergoglio had previously been Archbishop of Buenos Aires. He was the first pope from Latin America and the first Jesuit to hold the office.
q-gegenwart-36#question: Which eurozone country was the first to receive an international bailout package in the euro crisis in 2010?
q-gegenwart-36#explanation: In May 2010 EU states and the International Monetary Fund granted Greece billions in loans tied to strict austerity conditions. Ireland followed at the end of 2010 and Portugal in 2011.
q-gegenwart-37#question: Which artificial intelligence language program was used by millions of people within a few months from late 2022?
q-gegenwart-37#explanation: The company OpenAI released ChatGPT in November 2022. For the first time, generative AI became an everyday tool for a broad public.
q-gegenwart-38#question: What did the MeToo movement bring to worldwide attention from 2017?
q-gegenwart-38#choices.0: Sexual harassment and violence against women
q-gegenwart-38#explanation: Triggered by allegations against film producer Harvey Weinstein, millions of women shared their experiences under the slogan. Activist Tarana Burke had coined the phrase back in 2006.
q-gegenwart-39#question: Which organisation carried out the terrorist attack on Israel on 7 October 2023?
q-gegenwart-39#explanation: In the attack from the Gaza Strip, around 1,200 people in Israel were killed and more than 200 taken hostage. A war in the Gaza Strip with very many casualties followed.
q-gegenwart-40#question: In which Chinese city was the novel coronavirus first detected at the end of 2019?
q-gegenwart-40#explanation: From this city of millions in central China the virus spread worldwide; in March 2020 the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic. Lockdowns and vaccination campaigns shaped the following two years.
q-gegenwart-41#question: In which Mexican state did the Zapatistas rise up on 1 January 1994?
q-gegenwart-41#explanation: The indigenous rebels protested against poverty and marginalisation on the day NAFTA came into force. They named themselves after the revolutionary Emiliano Zapata.
q-gegenwart-42#question: Which state occupied East Timor from 1975 to 1999?
q-gegenwart-42#explanation: After the colonial power Portugal withdrew, Indonesia occupied the territory. In 1999 the population voted for independence, which became reality in 2002.
q-gegenwart-43#question: Which country became the first in the world to introduce same-sex marriage in 2001?
q-gegenwart-43#explanation: On 1 April 2001 the first same-sex couples were married in Amsterdam. Denmark had already allowed registered partnerships in 1989, and Canada and Spain followed with marriage in 2005.
q-gegenwart-44#question: In which country did the Asian financial crisis begin in 1997?
q-gegenwart-44#explanation: The crisis began in July 1997 with the collapse of the Thai currency, the baht, and then spread to Indonesia, South Korea and other countries. The International Monetary Fund provided emergency loans.
q-gegenwart-45#question: Which future prime minister, as finance minister, led the opening of India's economy in 1991?
q-gegenwart-45#explanation: During a severe balance-of-payments crisis, Singh cut tariffs and licensing requirements and opened India to foreign capital. He himself served as prime minister from 2004 to 2014.
q-gegenwart-46#question: Which agreement ended the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1995?
q-gegenwart-46#explanation: The warring parties negotiated the treaty in November 1995 at an air base in Dayton, Ohio. Bosnia and Herzegovina was preserved as a single state made up of two largely autonomous entities.
q-gegenwart-47#question: In which two fields were Nobel Prizes awarded in 2024 for research on artificial intelligence?
q-gegenwart-47#explanation: The Physics Prize went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for foundations of neural networks. The Chemistry Prize honoured, among other things, the AI-based prediction of protein structures.
q-gegenwart-48#question: Which country did China overtake in 2010 to become the world's second-largest economy?
q-gegenwart-48#explanation: After joining the WTO in 2001, China's economy grew at double-digit rates for years. After that, only the USA still had a larger economic output.
q-gegenwart-49#question: Which climate protection agreement was adopted in Japan in 1997?
q-gegenwart-49#explanation: For the first time industrialised countries committed themselves to binding limits on greenhouse gases. However, the USA never ratified the protocol; it was succeeded by the Paris Agreement of 2015.
q-gegenwart-50#question: Which of these events happened first?
q-gegenwart-50#explanation: The genocide in Rwanda took place in 1994. It was followed by the attacks of 11 September 2001, the global financial crisis of 2008 and the Arab Spring from late 2010.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-03#question: Who became president in South Africa's first free elections in 1994?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-03#explanation: Nelson Mandela, who had spent 27 years in prison, became the first black president of South Africa after the election victory of the ANC.
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-06#question: Which event triggered the global financial crisis in 2008?
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-06#choices.0: China's accession to the World Trade Organization
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-06#choices.2: The collapse of the bank Lehman Brothers
q-kalter-krieg-gegenwart-06#explanation: The bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers on September 15, 2008 shook the worldwide financial system.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-01#qu: Which invention is regarded as the most important driving force of the Industrial Revolution?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-01#ex: The steam engine, improved by James Watt, powered factories, locomotives and ships.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-02#qu: Who wrote the Communist Manifesto in 1848 together with Friedrich Engels?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-02#ex: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels published the Manifesto in London in February 1848.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-03#qu: In which year was the German Empire founded?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-03#ex: On January 18, 1871 Wilhelm I was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-04#qu: What was the result of the Meiji Restoration of 1868?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-04#ch: India became a British crown colony
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-04#ex: After the fall of the shogunate, Japan became an industrial power under Emperor Meiji within a single generation.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-05#qu: Which continent was divided among the European powers at the Berlin Conference of 1884/85?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-05#ex: The conference laid down rules for taking possession of African territory and set off the Scramble for Africa.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-06#qu: Which country had to cede Hong Kong to Great Britain after the First Opium War in 1842?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-06#ex: In the Treaty of Nanking China ceded Hong Kong and opened five ports to British trade.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-07#qu: Which country was the first in the world to introduce women's suffrage at the national level, in 1893?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-07#ex: After a petition with almost 32,000 signatures, the governor of New Zealand signed the electoral act on September 19, 1893.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-08#qu: Which book did Charles Darwin publish in 1859?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-08#ex: Darwin's main work explained the diversity of life through evolution and natural selection and sold out on the first day.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-09#qu: Who owned the Congo Free State from 1885 to 1908?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-09#ch: King Leopold II of Belgium as personal property
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-09#ex: Leopold II had the Congo exploited as his personal property; only after an international scandal did Belgium take over the colony in 1908.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-10#qu: Which insurance did the German Empire introduce in 1883 as its first social insurance?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-10#ex: Health insurance came in 1883, accident insurance in 1884 and old-age and disability insurance in 1889; unemployment insurance did not follow until 1927.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-11#qu: Which experience led Henry Dunant to found the Red Cross?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-11#ch: The wounded of the Battle of Solferino in 1859
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-11#ex: In 1859 Dunant witnessed the misery of the wounded after the Battle of Solferino and in his book called for voluntary aid societies and a protective convention.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-12#qu: What was the consequence of the Sepoy Rebellion of 1857 for India?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-12#ch: The British Crown took over rule from the East India Company
The Mughal emperor again ruled all of India
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-12#ex: After the rebellion was put down, the East India Company was dissolved in 1858 and India was placed directly under the British Crown.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-13#qu: How did James Watt decisively improve the steam engine?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-13#ex: Watt realized that Newcomen's engine wasted a great deal of energy; the separate condenser cut coal consumption by more than half. The unit of power, the watt, is named after him.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-14#qu: Which of these events happened first?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-14#ch: The first public steam railway runs between Stockton and Darlington
Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-14#ex: The Stockton and Darlington steam railway opened in 1825, the Communist Manifesto appeared in 1848, Darwin's book in 1859, and the Suez Canal opened in 1869.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-15#qu: Who patented the power loom in 1785?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-15#ex: Hargreaves had earlier developed the spinning jenny and Arkwright the water-powered water frame. Cartwright's loom now turned weaving into factory work as well.
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-16#qu: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin in the late 18th century?
q-industrialisierung-imperialismus-16#ex: Deposits of coal and iron, capital from overseas trade and large markets favored the breakthrough. Cities such as Manchester and Birmingham grew many times over within a few decades.
